raw_response:
I farm only 5 mu, so I will not spread myself too thin. I have done this a long time, and at my age I still start from what worked last year, then I change a little if I think it will pay. Around Quzhou, wheat and maize are the main steady crops, so I will keep most of my land in wheat-maize because that is the safest way to bring grain home. Cotton can still make some money, but it needs more watching and more spraying, so I will keep a smaller piece for cotton and not let it take over the farm. I have well water, so I will use that to protect the yield, especially for wheat at key times and for maize when the rain is short. On fertilizer, I would rather spend a bit more than leave the crop hungry. I went to primary school, so I do look at seed and fertilizer a bit more carefully than just guessing, but in the end I still trust what I have seen on our own land and what nearby farmers got good results with. I will use improved wheat seed, hybrid maize seed, and a better cotton variety, not old saved seed. I will keep the wheat and maize on 3 mu in rotation, and put 2 mu into cotton. That way the work and money are still manageable for my family, and I do not have to gamble too much on one crop.
